It's actually a common negotiating tactic to start with something unreasonable. It functions around a psychological phenomenon called "Anchoring". By opening up with "Deport all of the illegals", people immediately come to the defense of the good contributors and ask why they can't stay, rather than arguing that all of them should stay. He anchored the debate around deportation, and now all that's left is to decide who makes the cut.

The same thing is at work when you see a big price tag on an item slashed to a "reasonable" price. You feel like you're getting a much better deal when you see a $120 price tag with a slash and $59.99 tagged over it than you do when you see plain $59.99 price tag, because your brain is anchored to that $120 value.
